newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GMA to start 2nd phase of Mt Lyell study.
newsitem.headline: GMA to start 2nd phase of Mt Lyell study.

text.p: Gold Mines of Australia Ltd (GMA) said on Tuesday it would proceed with the second phase of its feasibility study into the use of bacterial oxidation to produce copper metal at its Mt Lyell mine in Tasmania.
The decision to move to the second phase follows the recent successful using of bacterial oxidation to extract copper metal from copper concentrate at a pilot plant at Mt Lyell, GMA said.
GMA chairman Andrew Love said in a statement if successful, the feasibility study could lead to use of the process on a commercial basis.
"We are encouraged by the success of phase one and will now continue with the next phase to determine the commercial viability of this process," Love said,
"If this operation does prove to be commercially viable, it will assist significantly in bringing Mt Lyell down the cost curve," he said.

The bacterial oxidation process has been successfully used to produce gold at GMA's Youanmi mine in Western Australia, but has not yet been commercially successful in extracting copper metal from copper concentrates.
The second phase of the study is expected to take up to nine months to complete, GMA said.
Mt Lyell produced copper at an average cost of US$0.92 a pound in 1996/97 (July/June) and is targeting a cost of US$0.85 in the current year, GMA secretary Ken Winters told Reuters.
Copper currently fetches about US$1.06 in international markets.
"Through bacterial oxidation we'd be looking a further stepped declines in costs of around 10 to 15 cents," he said.
